title: a key, token or password on a line the branch adds (the pinned secrets scanner)

explain.what: The pinned secrets scanner (gitleaks, tools/gitleaks) finds a key, token or password on a line the branch adds (LS/<its rule>). Only the file and the line are shown, never the value.
explain.why: The repo is public, and git keeps every pushed line in its history: once a key is pushed, anyone may already hold it. The scanner's own rules know the key formats; only what the branch adds is scanned.
explain.fix: Rotate the key first: revoke it where it was issued and make a new one. Removing the line is not enough - the value stays in the git history and may already be copied. Read the new key from the environment, never a repo file. A false positive needs a waiver for LS/<rule>.
